2028 Mitsubishi Outlander Diamond Trail Edition: How Does It Compare to Other Adventure Crossovers?
14 photos
Photo: Mitsubishi
Mitsubishi Motors North America ( MMNA ) revealed ahead of the 2026 edition of the SEMA Show (November 3 to 6) its triumphant return to Las Vegas, Nevada, for the first time since 2012. The Japanese company’s subsidiary also has a headline – the 2028 Outlander Diamond Trail Edition.
We’ve said it on numerous occasions: quite sadly, right now the Japanese automaker’s US subsidiary is a pale shadow of a shadow of its former self . If you need an eloquent example, earlier this month they reported a total of just 18,543 sales during the third quarter of 2026, and after that the only novelty has been the reveal of the pricing details for the Nissan Leaf-based 2027 Mitsubishi Eclipse Sportback. The new fastback EV starts at an MSRP of almost $38k, which is considerably higher than its corporate sibling, which kicks off at less than $30k for the 2026 model year.
Most likely they won’t improve their sales too much with this new model, but at least we have higher hopes for the new 2028 Outlander Diamond Trail Edition , which is an adventure version of their best-selling nameplate. The trail-focused version of its three-row crossover is coming as a triple example at the SEMA Show, one stock with Mitsubishi Genuine Accessories and a color-matched Thule roof box, one packing more goodies, and the third one as extreme as possible.
Back to the regular version, the new trim levels come with a new Rock off-road mode for the Super-All Wheel Control System, modified bumpers which enable improved approach and departure angles from 18.3 to 20.5 degrees and from 22.2 to 23.1 degrees, all-terrain tires, and new wheels: 18-inch black alloy wheels with dedicated Nexen Roadian ATXs.
Photo: Mitsubishi Inside, there’s off-road feedback through the dedicated instrument-cluster display screen in Rock mode, showing things like the steering angle, individual wheel slip, and traction-control intervention in real time, while the Multi-View Camera System also acts differently and stays active up to 18.6 mph or 30 kph instead of the standard 6.2mph/10kph threshold.
There is also a unique water-repelling dark grey material with khaki stitching for the upholstery, as well as textured matte black, dark chrome, and dark satin trim elements. The new Diamond Trail Edition logo is also present, on the seat backs, floor mats, and the door card. Last but not least, Mitsubishi introduces a new color, Trail Green Metallic, highlighting the Diamond Trail Edition.
Mitsubishi hasn’t revealed any additional technical characteristics or the pricing details and the release date, but we can easily see the 2028 model year of the Mitsubishi Outlander take on the flurry of compact crossover SUV adventurers like the Ford Bronco Sport Badlands, Jeep Compass Trailhawk, Toyota RAV4 Woodland, Honda CR-V TrailSport Hybrid, Hyundai Tucson XRT, Kia Sportage X-Pro, Subaru Forester Wilderness, and also the Nissan Rogue Rock Creek Edition, of course.
Photo: Mitsubishi All of them come with a ton of adventure-focused tips and tricks. The Nissan Rogue Rock Creek has standard AWD, exclusive styling perks, water-repellent seats, HDC, and an HD Intelligent Around View Monitor, among other things, with the standard 1.5-liter VC-Turbo 3-cylinder engine still packed under the hood with 201 hp and 225 lb-ft of torque.
The Toyota RAV4 Woodland is even more capable than the Nissan because it has a standard 236-hp hybrid powertrain and the optional 324-hp plug-in hybrid option. It also comes with rugged features: increased ground clearance, a TRD-tuned suspension, all-terrain tires, and 18-inch wheels. The Hyundai Tucson XRT is also available as a hybrid and leans heavily into the adventure look from the get-go, but you should always also consider its sibling, the Kia Sportage X-Pro (gasoline) or Sportage X-Line Hybrid, before making a choice.
We shouldn’t forget about the newly introduced Honda CR-V TrailSport Hybrid or the recently launched Subaru Forester Wilderness, which is now also available with the hybrid powertrain, or about the American greats, the Ford Bronco Sport Badlands and the Jeep Cherokee Trailhawk Hybrid. One thing is for sure: the 2028 Mitsubishi Outlander Diamond Trail Edition will have its work cut out for it because most carmakers offer an adventure-focused version of their most popular compact crossover SUVs across the US automotive market right now.
Photo: Mitsubishi Interestingly, we don’t believe that Mitsubishi chose the SEMA Show in Las Vegas for nothing, as the stock example is joined by another two units that feature increasingly complicated off-road-focused configurations with extra goodies from across the aftermarket realm. The second Mitsu BF Goodrich Trail Terrain T/A tires sized 265/65-18, a Thule Caprock roof rack packing two Specialized StumpJumper 15 mountain bikes, as well as an Anderson Design & Fabrication 1.5-inch lift kit.
There’s also accessory lighting from Rough Country, as well as a matching custom-painted GulfStream Trail Boss 1090K trailer. The third one is even more extreme, packing 18 by 8.5-inch Method Race Wheels 707s, T/A K03s, a 2.5-inch suspension lift via Flatout Suspension's GR Lite strut kit with adjustable spring perches, a Thule Caprock roof rack topped with a Thule Approach 2M rooftop tent and Rough Country traction boards, plus a Rough Country accessory light bar and light pods. 2026 SEMA Show • 2027 Dodge Charger Gets Special-Edition Package Celebrating 90 Years of Mopar
Rare 1968 Dodge Hemi Charger R/T Selling at No Reserve, One of 211 Made
17 photos
Photo: Mecum Auctions
Introduced in January 1966, the Dodge Charger was the first Mopar to receive the street-spec version of the 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi V8 engine . The 425-horsepower mill remained on the Charger's options list through 1971.
The Charger wasn't a big seller in its first two years on the market. Originally an upscale fastback, it moved about 37,344 units in 1966 and only 15,788 examples in 1967. In 1968, the Charger returned as a more conventional muscle car, and sales exceeded 96,000 units.
Sales remained strong in 1969 and reached nearly 50,000 units in 1970. The latter was a poor year for muscle cars, so that figure is rather high. Dodge also managed to move over 45,000 Chargers in 1971, at a time when performance cars were struggling to find new homes.
In all, Dodge sold over 300,000 Chargers between 1966 and 1971, but only a tiny fraction of them were equipped with the 426 Hemi V8 . Records show that only 1,487 cars got the said powerplant, accounting for a minuscule 0.5% of the total production. Unsurprisingly, these rare vehicles are very desirable nowadays.
The 1968 version is the most common, with 475 examples made. The Charger R/T you see here is one of those cars. But because it was ordered with a four-speed manual transmission, it's actually one of 211 units built. The other 264 were ordered with the three-speed TorqueFlite automatic.
A blue-on-blue classic, this Charger looks near perfect inside and out, a sign that it may have been restored in recent years. However, it's still highly original in terms of sheet metal and drivetrain components. It has the correct dual-quad Carter carburetor setup, as well as a Dana 60 rear end with 3.54 gears.
The Charger was recently included among the lots that are scheduled to go under the hammer at Mecum's Kissimmee 2027 auction in January. And what makes it particularly interesting is that it will be sold at no reserve. That's quite rare for Hemi Mopars , which usually hit the block with reserved prices (a safety net for the sellers).
Even so, this Charger should change hands for a six-figure sum. As of this writing, the 10 most expensive 1968 Hemi Chargers ever auctioned off fetched between $123,750 and $302,500. The record holder is a Burgundy Metallic unit that went under the hammer in 2026.
Internet records show that this particular Charger was previously sold in 2018 for $113,400. In March 2023, it crossed the block at Glendale for $214,500. All told, it's already among the most expensive units ever sold at public auction. How much do you think it will go for this time around ? Check it out in the photo gallery and let me know in the comments section below.

Keyvany’s New G850 Is a Mercedes-AMG G 63 That Looks Like a Confused Mansory
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | keyvany
Is it a bird? Is it a plane? Nope, it’s just another tuned G-Wagen that looks like it tries too much to be a Mansory. However, it has nothing to do with the latter company, because, as mentioned above, this project came directly from Keyvany’s portfolio.
Following in the footsteps of other brash builds that this tuner has recently signed, it does not look kitschy on the outside, but then again, you can blame it on the glossy black overall look. That’s because this color tends to hide bold makeovers like a champ, and we reckon that if this thing were presented in a more vibrant color, joined by some forged carbon accents, then the word “kitschy” would have been found in the title.
Keyvany surely knows how to attract attention, and its latest take on the Mercedes- AMG G 63 is definitely a head-turner, albeit not for the right reasons. That’s because it tries too much to look beastly. But then again, we have seen far worse takes on the modern-day G-Wagen over the years, including some from this company, like the so-called G950 that we covered here a little over a month ago, which had a similar makeover, albeit with a different exterior color.
This ride is called the Keyvany G850, and is said to be an entirely new project. It features redesigned fender flares that are not necessarily better looking than the stock ones, as well as new side skirts with cutouts in front of the rear wheels for the side-exit exhaust tips, which are now three instead of two on each side. The front fender trim is new, there is a splitter attached to the front bumper, and chances are that the latter component has also come from the tuner’s shelves.
Photo: Instagram | keyvany We can also see that the grille of this tuned Mercedes-AMG G 63 has also come from Keyvany’s portfolio. It has different slats, and the tuner’s logo sits right in the middle. The hood is on the more muscular side of things, as it has a big scoop right in the middle. The central part of the front bumper is home to an aftermarket light strip, and we can see another one mounted above the front windscreen.
It looks like there are some aftermarket panels on the sides, thus contributing to this vehicle’s wider overall nature, and there are also some fake vents behind the rear fender flares. The rear bumper seems to be entirely new as well, and it features a new diffuser attached to it that extends on the lower part toward the car’s sides. The double-bubble-like roof spoiler is another novelty, just like the trim on the rear pillars, and the custom spare wheel holder attached t othe rear door.
Keyvany’s logos decorate various parts of the exterior, and this modified Mercedes-AMG G 63 also sits a bit closer to the asphalt, suggesting that a lowering kit is part of the makeover. The concave wheels are also new, and while they are not exactly the most inspiring, we’ve seen worse choices. Like far worse.
Our better halves know what the interior color is called, but to us, it’s an orange-y theme, joined by new trim, the Keyvany logo on various components, new seatbelts, redesigned seats, and a few other bits and bobs that make this modern-day G-Wagen stand out more. And this is definitely one vibrant-looking cockpit, though it does not necessarily fit the design of this model, does it?
Photo: Instagram | keyvany Either way, the tuner’s work hasn’t ended here, because this Mercedes-AMG G 63 also has more power. The G850 in its name reveals that the revised output is now rated at 850 metric horsepower, which equals 838 brake horsepower and 625 kilowatts. The acceleration and top speed haven’t been mentioned at the time of writing, but then again, Keyvany did not have much to say about this build, as you can see from the social media post embedded at the bottom of the page.
As for the standard Mercedes-AMG G 63, it comes with 577 hp (585 ps/430 kW) and 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque from its 4.0-liter bi-turbocharged V8 engine. The lump drives all four wheels through a nine-speed automatic transmission, and the automaker reveals that 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) takes as little as 4.2 seconds, which is impressive, given that this model is anything but a blue-blooded crossover. In fact, it’s a body-on-frame truck that will hit 137 mph 9220 kph) flat-out, or 149 mph (240 kph) with the optional AMG Performance Pack.
One must fork out a minimum of $198,750 for a brand-new Mercedes-AMG G 63 from the 2027 model year, before destination, options, and dealer fees, and a lot more if they somehow dream about owning a Keyvany, because these things may not be the prettiest G-Wagens out there, but they do cost a pretty penny. Would you ever see yourself driving one of these? View this post on Instagram A post shared by ® (@keyvany)

This Stealthy Toyota Sienna Micro Camper Van Packs a Surprisingly Flexible Living Space Inside
20 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Josh Oakes
Transforming an area that's smaller than an averagely sized full bathroom into a livable space is quite the challenge. However, you can always count on human creativity to come up with all sorts of solutions, just like the clever use of space inside the micro camper van I'd like to discuss today.
What we have here is a project based on a 2025 Toyota Sienna – I've seen an increasing number of Sienna-based conversions lately.
This micro camper van is the work of Josh Oakes. Working under Briarwood Vans, his Madison, Wisconsin-based company, Josh specializes in full camper van conversions, build plans and DIY consulting for such projects. He works mostly with small vans, but he has also done larger conversions, such as this ProMaster .
Looking at the rig from the outside, it won't tell you that much. In terms of exterior upgrades, you'll notice a flexible 200 W solar panel, a shore power hookup integrated into the rear bumper, and a few red LED lights on the same rear bumper.
That means the majority of people will look at the van and think it's a simple passenger van, making it suitable for some stealth camping.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Josh Oakes Once you step inside, it's clear that this isn't any ordinary vehicle. By the way, the van comes with two sliding doors – Josh said that the one on the driver's side is the entrance, as the other one is slightly blocked by the kitchen. However, you can technically step inside through either door.
Regarding aesthetics, you'll notice grey vinyl flooring, pine plywood cabinetry, and grey cushion upholstery. The look is complemented by multiple light sources.
The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. There is some separation created between the two areas due to the kitchen, which sits right behind the driver and passenger seats.
The kitchen features a round sink with a rechargeable electric faucet and a cover, two AC outlets, a cabinet with a hinged top that houses a chest-style fridge, three drawers with locking slides, and a cabinet underneath the sink. There's also a flip-down door that can be opened to reveal a battery monitor and an inverter controller.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Josh Oakes You can access the latter through another door from the passenger side. It holds a straightforward plumbing system made up of two removable canisters, one for fresh water and the other for grey water.
The nicest and funniest touch in the kitchen is a clothes holder with three hooks in the shape of dog butts with tails. Above them, there's a tiny shelf for bits and bobs.
The rest of the living space is taken up by a smartly built bed and bench platform. In the day setup (or the setup meant for sitting), you get two benches with backrests.
Two people can sit in the front part of the platform. However, you can keep the trunk door open and have two more people sitting in the back, mirroring the position of those in the front.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Josh Oakes Setting up the bed or a lounge area is super easy and quick – the platform has two sliding panels, so all you need to do is fold them flat by pulling them out. The result is a sleeping arrangement that's 48 inches (122 centimeters) wide and 72 inches (183 centimeters) long.
Alternatively, you can fold flat just one of the two parts so one person can lay down and the other can stay seated. What's more, you get a decent amount of storage space underneath the bed.
The platform's back panel is hinged, allowing you to lift it and reveal a large storage space. You can also set it up at an angle to create a sort of daybed.
Josh created two side walls. The one on the passenger side has a storage cubby that also allows you to access the factory cup holders and two USB-C charging points. The other one is mostly the same, except it also has two switches for the rear LED lights I mentioned earlier and for recessed LED light strips inside the van.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Josh Oakes "How about the utility systems?" you might be wondering. Josh cleverly hid the electrical system inside the bench/bed, underneath the top panels. The van is equipped with a 200 Ah battery bank and a 2,000 W inverter.
All in all, Josh and Briarwood Vans created a seemingly simple yet ingenious living space using so little space. Sure, it's not suitable for full-time living, but it can certainly offer a great amount of comfort for a weekend adventure.
There's one more detail that makes this project even better. The entire bed system, the cabinets, and even the subfloor can be removed, as they're attached to the factory mounting points. That means that you could reinstall the second and third row seating if you wanted to.
